The dissociation of the Ca-EDTA complex is given by:  
\[
\text{CaY}^{2-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{Y}^{4-}
\]  
with formation constant \(K = \frac{[\text{CaY}^{2-}]}{[\text{Ca}^{2+}][\text{Y}^{4-}]} = 5 \times 10^{10}\).  
Initial concentration of complex is 0.02 M. Let \(x = [\text{Ca}^{2+}] = [\text{Y}^{4-}]\) at equilibrium. Then  
\[
\frac{0.02 - x}{x^2} = 5 \times 10^{10}.
\]  
Since \(K\) is large, \(x\) is very small, so \(0.02 - x \approx 0.02\). Thus  
\[
\frac{0.02}{x^2} = 5 \times 10^{10} \quad \Rightarrow \quad x^2 = \frac{0.02}{5 \times 10^{10}} = 4 \times 10^{-13},
\]  
\[
x = \sqrt{4 \times 10^{-13}} = 2 \times 10^{-6.5} \approx 6.3 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{M}.
\]  
The approximation is valid, so the concentration of calcium ions is \(6.3 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{M}\).
